errors.title: The terminal can't find Ollama
errors.cause: Ollama is not installed yet, or this terminal window was opened before the install finished, so it does not know where Ollama is.
fix: Close this terminal completely and open a new one.
Run `ollama --version` again.
If it still fails, repeat the install step and watch for error messages.
Windows: restart the PC once if a new terminal does not help. This refreshes the PATH setting.
Linux and macOS: run `which ollama` to see whether the program exists.

errors.title: Ollama is installed but its server is not running
patterns: could not connect to a running Ollama
(connection refused|econnrefused|failed to connect|unable to connect|couldn't connect).*(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1|11434)
unable to connect to the remote server
errors.cause: Ollama works as a small background server. The commands talk to it, and right now nothing is answering on port 11434.
fix: Windows and macOS: open the Ollama app from the Start menu or Applications and wait a few seconds.
Any system: open a second terminal, run `ollama serve`, and keep that window open.
Linux with systemd: run `systemctl status ollama` and, if it is stopped, run `sudo systemctl start ollama`.
Then test again with `curl http://localhost:11434` (Windows: `Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:11434`).

errors.title: Port 11434 is already in use
patterns: only one usage of each socket address
errors.cause: Another copy of Ollama, or another program, is already using the port Ollama needs. Most often Ollama is simply already running, which is fine.
fix: First test whether Ollama already works: `curl http://localhost:11434` (Windows: `Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:11434`). If it says "Ollama is running", skip `ollama serve` and carry on.
Windows: find the program using the port with `netstat -ano | findstr 11434`.
Linux and macOS: find it with `lsof -i :11434`.
Quit the extra Ollama copy (tray icon, then Quit) and start Ollama once.

errors.title: Ollama doesn't know that model name
patterns: pull model manifest: file does not exist
errors.cause: The model name or tag is misspelled, or that tag does not exist in the Ollama library.
fix: Check the exact name and tag on https://ollama.com/library (for example `gemma3:1b`).
Names use a colon between model and size: `llama3.2:3b`, not `llama3.2-3b`.
See what you already have with `ollama list`.
Copy the command from this page again instead of retyping it.

errors.title: Your computer doesn't have enough memory for this model
errors.cause: Models are loaded fully into RAM or GPU memory. This one is bigger than what is free right now.
fix: Close browsers and other heavy programs, then try again.
Go back to the model list and pick a smaller model marked "Fast" or "Runs on your CPU".
Small versions such as `gemma3:1b` or `llama3.2:1b` need about 4 GB of RAM.
Restart the computer to free memory if it has been on for days.

errors.title: There isn't enough free disk space
patterns: there is not enough space on the disk
errors.cause: The download needs room for the whole model plus some working space, and the drive is almost full.
fix: Free up at least the model size plus 2 GB: empty the recycle bin or bin and delete large unused files.
Remove models you no longer need with `ollama rm <model>` (see them with `ollama list`).
Run the same `ollama pull` command again. The download resumes where it stopped.
Still tight? Choose a smaller model.

errors.title: The download failed because of a network problem
errors.cause: Ollama could not finish talking to the download servers. This is usually a weak connection, a VPN, or a school or office firewall.
fix: Check your internet and run the same `ollama pull` command again. Downloads resume where they stopped.
Turn off any VPN, or switch to another network such as a phone hotspot.
College and office Wi-Fi often block large downloads. Try a different network.
A certificate (x509) error means the network is inspecting secure traffic. Use a different network.

errors.title: PowerShell is blocking the script
patterns: cannot be loaded because running scripts
errors.cause: Windows can restrict which PowerShell scripts may run. This is a safety setting, not a fault with your PC.
fix: In the same PowerShell window run `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned`. It only affects the current window.
Run the install command again in that window.
Or skip the script and download the installer from https://ollama.com/download.

errors.title: You need administrator (sudo) rights
errors.cause: Installing system software needs administrator rights, and this account or command does not have them.
fix: Run the install again and type your password when `sudo` asks. Nothing shows while you type, which is normal.
Your account must be allowed to use sudo. On a shared or school computer ask the administrator.
If you cannot get admin rights, use a personal computer for this.

errors.title: Windows needs administrator rights
errors.cause: The install needs to change system settings and PowerShell was not opened as an administrator.
fix: Close PowerShell.
Press Start, type PowerShell, right-click it and choose Run as administrator.
Run the install command again.

errors.title: curl is not installed
errors.cause: The install command downloads Ollama with a tool called curl, which this system does not have yet.
fix: Ubuntu or Debian: `sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y curl`
Fedora: `sudo dnf install -y curl`
Arch: `sudo pacman -S curl`
Then run the install command again.

errors.title: There is a problem with the graphics card (GPU) setup
errors.cause: Ollama tried to use your NVIDIA GPU but the driver is missing, outdated or mismatched. Ollama can still run on the CPU, only more slowly.
fix: Update the NVIDIA driver from nvidia.com or your laptop maker, then restart the computer.
Check that the card is visible with `nvidia-smi`.
No NVIDIA GPU? That is not an error. Models simply run on the CPU.
Meanwhile choose a smaller model so CPU speed is acceptable.

errors.title: The model process crashed
errors.cause: The part of Ollama that runs the model stopped unexpectedly. The usual causes are too little memory or a GPU driver problem.
fix: Try a smaller model.
Update Ollama by installing it again, then check `ollama --version`.
Update your GPU driver and restart the computer.
Restart the server: quit Ollama and start it again, or run `ollama serve`.

errors.title: Python is not installed or not on your PATH
errors.cause: Python is missing, or the terminal does not know where it is.
fix: Install Python 3.10 or newer from https://www.python.org/downloads/ (on Windows tick "Add python.exe to PATH").
Close and reopen the terminal.
Windows uses `python --version`, macOS and Linux use `python3 --version`.
If the Microsoft Store opens, turn off the python alias under Settings, Apps, Advanced app settings, App execution aliases.

errors.title: Your Python version is too old
errors.cause: Most AI libraries need Python 3.10 or newer.
fix: Install the latest Python from https://www.python.org/downloads/.
Reopen the terminal and check again.

errors.title: Git is not installed
errors.cause: Git is missing, or the terminal does not know where it is.
fix: Download it from https://git-scm.com/downloads and install it with the default options.
On Ubuntu or Debian you can run `sudo apt install -y git`.
Close and reopen the terminal, then check again.

errors.title: macOS blocked the app
patterns: is damaged and can't be opened
errors.cause: macOS asks you to confirm apps that were downloaded from the internet.
fix: Open System Settings, then Privacy & Security, scroll down and click "Open Anyway" next to Ollama.
Download Ollama only from https://ollama.com/download.
Move Ollama into the Applications folder and open it again.

errors.title: systemd is not available (common in WSL and containers)
patterns: system has not been booted with systemd
errors.cause: This Linux environment does not run background services the usual way, so Ollama cannot start itself.
fix: Start Ollama by hand in a second terminal window with `ollama serve`.
Leave that window open while you use `ollama pull` and `ollama run` in the first one.

errors.title: The model is very slow
errors.cause: Large models on a computer without a strong GPU generate text slowly because the CPU does all the work. The very first answer is also slower because the model has to load.
fix: Use a smaller model (1B to 4B parameters).
Close other programs to free memory.
Check whether your GPU is used: run `ollama ps` while a model is loaded and read the PROCESSOR column.
Give the first answer a minute. Later answers are faster.

errors.title: The download seems stuck
errors.cause: Models are several gigabytes and speed varies a lot. Short pauses near the end are normal while Ollama checks the files.
fix: Wait a few minutes. Watch whether the numbers still change.
If nothing moves for 5 minutes, press Ctrl+C and run the same `ollama pull` command again. It resumes.
Try another network or turn off your VPN.
Pick a smaller model if your connection is slow.
